_dataset_notes.purpose: Synthetic demo/test dataset for ClaimGuard AI (hackathon prototype). All names, addresses, policy numbers, and claim details are fictional — generated for testing only, not real customer data.

scenario_coverage.clean_claims: CG-001 to CG-024 (24 claims) — varied incident types, amounts, and channels, including deliberately high-value but well-documented claims so the system proves it isn't just flagging by amount.
scenario_coverage.consistency_mismatches: CG-025 to CG-030 (6 claims) — photo/narrative mismatches at low, medium, and high severity.
scenario_coverage.repeat_claimant_pattern: CG-031 to CG-033 (3 claims, same claimant_id) — legitimate-looking but frequent claims from one claimant.
scenario_coverage.shared_address_ring: CG-034 to CG-036 (3 claims, different claimant_ids, same address) — potential collusion/staged-ring signal.
scenario_coverage.claim_frequency_spike: CG-037 to CG-039 (3 claims, same claimant, all within 45 days) — velocity-based fraud signal.
scenario_coverage.policy_date_anomaly: CG-040, CG-041 (2 claims) — incident_date precedes policy_start_date (classic backdating/antedating fraud pattern).
scenario_coverage.duplicate_submission: CG-042 — resubmission of an already-paid claim under a new claim_number, same policy_number and incident details.

_dataset_notes.usage_tip: Load into Firestore as the seed collection before your demo. For the video, use CG-025 (high severity mismatch) as your primary flagged example, and CG-031/034/037 to show each distinct pattern-flag type separately. CG-030 intentionally combines a medium consistency flag with membership in the CG-034 address ring.
_dataset_notes.damage_photo_field: Filenames are placeholders — pair each with a real or stock image matching (or, for mismatch claims, deliberately NOT matching) the damage_description before uploading, since your Extraction/Consistency agents need actual image content to reason over.
